q: Oxidation numbers have a variety of uses in chemistry- from writing formulae to predicting properties of compounds and assisting in the balancing of ____ reactions in which electrons are transferred.
e: Oxidation numbers are essential for balancing redox reactions where electron transfer occurs.

q: The ____ (or oxidation state) of an atom can be zero, positive, or negative.
e: The oxidation number represents the number of electrons lost or gained by an atom.

q: All elements in their free state (uncombined with other elements) have an oxidation number of ____.
e: Free neutral atoms have the same number of electrons assigned to them as in their free state, resulting in an oxidation number of zero.

q: A positive oxidation number means the atom has ____ electrons assigned to it than in the neutral atom.
e: A positive oxidation number indicates the number of electrons removed from a neutral atom.

q: A negative oxidation number means the atom has ____ electrons assigned to it than in the neutral atom.
e: A negative oxidation number indicates the number of electrons added to a neutral atom.

q: The oxidation number of an atom that has lost or gained electrons to form an ion is the same as the positive or negative ____ of the ion.
e: The oxidation state of a monatomic ion is equal to its net electrical charge.

q: All elements regardless of whether they are monoatomic, diatomic or triatomic have an oxidation number of ____.
e: Elements in their free, uncombined state always have an oxidation number of zero.

q: The algebraic sum of the oxidation numbers of the atoms in a neutral molecule is ____.
e: For any electrically neutral compound, the sum of all oxidation numbers must equal zero.

q: The algebraic sum of the oxidation numbers of the atoms in a polyatomic ion is equal to the ____ on the ion.
e: The sum of oxidation numbers in a polyatomic ion must equal the net charge of that ion.

q: Oxidation number of H is ____, except in metal hydrides, where it is -1.
e: Hydrogen generally has an oxidation number of +1 when combined with nonmetals.

q: Oxidation number of H in metal hydrides is ____.
e: In metal hydrides like NaH or CaH2, hydrogen is more electronegative than the metal and takes an oxidation state of -1.

q: Oxidation number of O is ____, except in peroxides and in $OF_2$.
e: Oxygen typically has an oxidation number of -2 in most of its compounds.

q: Oxidation number of O in peroxides (e.g., $H_2O_2$, $BaO_2$, $Na_2O_2$) is ____.
e: In peroxide compounds, the oxygen atoms share a different bonding arrangement, resulting in an oxidation state of -1.

q: Oxidation number of O in $OF_2$ is ____.
e: Fluorine is more electronegative than oxygen, so oxygen takes a positive oxidation state of +2 in $OF_2$.

q: The metallic element in an ionic compound has a ____ oxidation number.
e: Metals tend to lose electrons to form cations, resulting in a positive oxidation number.

q: Alkali metals in combined state have an oxidation number ____.
e: Group 1 alkali metals always exhibit an oxidation state of +1 in their compounds.

q: Alkaline earth metals in combined state have an oxidation number ____.
e: Group 2 alkaline earth metals always exhibit an oxidation state of +2 in their compounds.

q: The oxidation number of halogen in compounds (e.g., $BaCl_2$, $NaBr$, $KI$) is ____.
e: Halogens typically have an oxidation number of -1 when combined with less electronegative elements.

q: In covalent compounds, the negative oxidation number is assigned to the more ____ atom.
e: Electrons in a covalent bond are assigned to the more electronegative atom for the purpose of determining oxidation numbers.
